content: In 2019, a comprehensive survey was conducted in Serbia to assess water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH) conditions across 320 healthcare facilities. This survey, carried out over two months, utilized on-site observations, structured interviews, and water quality testing to evaluate microbiological and chemical parameters. Additionally, a qualitative assessment was performed to analyze the enabling environment, which included a desk review of policies and implementation mechanisms, as well as semi-structured interviews with key stakeholders at various levels. The results of this initiative highlighted several key outcomes and impacts. There was improved collaboration between different departments within the Ministry of Health responsible for WASH services, environmental cleaning, and waste management. Furthermore, stronger partnerships were established between the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Environment to address waste and wastewater management. Plans were initiated to develop practical guidelines to support policy implementation, particularly in the areas of water supply operation and maintenance, hygiene, cleaning, and waste management in healthcare facilities. WASH was also integrated into a new Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) rulebook, fostering better collaboration between WASH, IPC, and patient safety departments at the facility level. The survey identified the need for structured training materials and guidance to help healthcare facilities comply with legal WASH requirements. A review of existing national targets was conducted, leading to the formulation of dedicated WASH targets for healthcare facilities within the framework of the European UNECE/WHO Protocol on Water and Health. Advanced WASH service level indicators were developed to be incorporated into routine surveillance and monitoring systems, enabling progress reporting toward Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 6. Additionally, the Ministry of Health committed to integrating WASH into the national Antimicrobial Resistance (AMR) plan during its next review, which occurs every three years. A situational analysis was emphasized as a critical tool for decision-makers, providing the necessary knowledge and evidence to take concrete actions to improve WASH in healthcare facilities. The findings were intended to inform the development of national targets and a roadmap for achieving universal and sustainable access to quality healthcare, as recommended in the 2019 Resolution on WASH in healthcare facilities. Experiences from other countries demonstrated that such analyses are effective in bringing together diverse stakeholders to jointly analyze and address challenges, leading to a more comprehensive understanding of the factors, gaps, and solutions for improving and sustaining WASH in healthcare settings. The approach for conducting a situational analysis of WASH and quality in healthcare facilities included several practical steps. These steps involved examining health and WASH policies, governance structures, and funding streams, as well as assessing WASH coverage and compliance. Community engagement was also prioritized, recognizing the role of community members in defining, demanding, and providing feedback on health services. The analysis also highlighted the importance of setting clear targets and defining a roadmap for WASH improvements, supported by an intersectoral national team. The development of the health workforce was emphasized, with training on WASH and IPC practices included in pre-service education and professional development. Operational research and knowledge sharing were encouraged to test and scale innovative approaches and refine programmatic strategies. Core questions for monitoring WASH in healthcare facilities were adapted from the WHO/UNICEF Joint Monitoring Programme’s framework, covering aspects such as water sources, toilet availability, waste management, and cleaning protocols. Indicators were graded using a traffic-light system to assess the enabling environment for WASH, with green indicating full compliance, orange indicating partial compliance or significant shortcomings, and red indicating non-compliance. The analysis also explored the integration of WASH into broader health policies, such as quality care, universal health coverage, maternal and child health, AMR, and climate policies. Political leadership and institutional arrangements were identified as critical factors for accelerating WASH improvements. At the facility level, strategies for quality improvement, WASH, IPC, and patient safety were assessed. The analysis examined the availability of funding, alignment with national and regional directions, and mechanisms for learning and feedback. The role of the community in supporting WASH improvements was also explored, with recommendations for empowering community members to demand and support higher-quality services. Overall, the situational analysis provided a comprehensive framework for understanding barriers to quality care and identifying actionable steps to improve WASH in healthcare facilities. It emphasized the importance of collaboration, evidence-based decision-making, and sustained investment to achieve universal access to quality healthcare.
